$comment: Provenance for every figure in docs/diagrams/. Checked by tools/check-manifest.py; see README.md §2 for why. `sources` are the files a figure derives its facts from — a deleted one fails, a changed one warns. `evidence` declares which of a figure's content is measured, read from source, or illustrative, because a reader cannot tell those apart by looking. `generates` lists frames exported from a substrate, which inherit provenance rather than carrying their own.

figures.shows: Muster on the Logos stack: three entry points over app backends, modules, network and runtime, with a dark band for the infrastructure the user does not run. Seven selectable views, including the demo build and the specified build as an A/B.

sources.note: the module set and its declared dependencies
which inputs are pinned and which follow chat_module's own
what the demo composes, and the invariant-by-invariant table behind the demo-build view
the specified build, the three hosts, ADR-008
the mixnet status this diagram refuses to overstate

evidence.note: The module set and every dependency edge, read off metadata.json and flake.nix rather than drawn from memory
LOGOS-MIXNET at status raw, send-only proof of concept, absent from the near-term roadmap — dated 2026-08 and shown as not shipped. muster-module.lgx is dashed for the same reason: P0 has not run
The neighbouring platform pieces (Files, Swaps, Dex, Storage) place Muster in context; they are not an enumeration of the platform's modules

figures.recheck: Every phase. P0 landing makes muster-module real and it stops being dashed; ADR-010's resolution may remove the chat_module box entirely; any movement on LOGOS-MIXNET changes the network layer.

figures.shows: The keystone: seven pipeline stages against what runs each conventionally and who operates that, what runs it here, and who still sees what. Nine views — per-use-case retellings, three that select by observer rather than by stage, and one that marks the two stages left unassessed.

figures.recheck: Every phase, and before any post using it publishes. The two unassessed cells become assessable only when the zone answers on mempool visibility and the production sequencer model; the contracting row changes when F-4/FS-6 land.

figures.shows: The account-id derivation drawn: id is a function of a viewing key and an identifier, the published keys carry no identifier, so the sender's client picks one at random and the note lands where nobody is looking. Plus the workaround and its two disclosed costs.

evidence.note: Reproduced twice — two peers over the testnet and a single-process standalone reproducer. The two account ids and their balances are the observed values
The derivation from (viewing key, identifier) and the random choice are read off wallet_ffi and lez_core, whose own comment states the random pick

figures.recheck: When the upstream issue is fixed. At that point the workaround comes out of the build and this figure becomes history rather than a caveat — which is worth drawing the difference between.
